findings.summary: Each build's Ninja dependency log is read once, concurrently, and also serves the precompiled-header freshness check through one parser and one newerInput rule.
One commandOutput helper reads /Fo, /Fo:, a separated /Fo and -o for the precompiled-header outputs and the lint cache.
lintCompilationGroups returns the key it computed; result keys and inputs are computed only for the unit that runs, with one stat per path per run.
Both caches identify files with the shared inputIdentity, hash with hashEntries and read the environment through environmentValue.
The lint result key is built from the clang-tidy executable's identity and the arguments it runs with.
One unused-for-N-days prune serves both caches daily and clean --cache-days, which also reports them.
The fixture cache has one entry point owning /showIncludes and its notes; the plan exposes its sources instead of a second source pattern.
Fixture keys include CL, _CL_, LINK and _LINK_ and the libraries a /LIBPATH: folder supplies.
Stored fixture headers carry their size and time, so a hit rereads only changed headers, and a new build replaces older variants of its command.
Paths inside the checkout enter both caches' keys relative to it, and setup-worktree shares both caches.
A linking fixture command stores only its executable, and the unused stored output list and refusals no fixture reaches are removed.
